main_text.p: Ezechiel in Babylone eadem docuit & prædixit quæ Jeremias in Judæa & Jerusalem, nempe Dominum effecturum, ut urbs propter ipsorum idololatriam & flagitia obsidione prematur, multi in ea fame & peste pereant. Eadem minatur illis qui iam abducti, & mox abducendi erant. Capite 4. maiori vehementia rem agit, jubet enim Deus prophetam urbem delineare super laterem, eam obsidere & toto obsidionis tempore panem ex tritico, hordeo, faba, lente, milio, siligine confecto, certo pondere vesci, aquam certa mensura bibere, loco prunarum, quibus panem coquebat, stercus humanum accipere, aut pro humano, fimum boum. Quibus omnibus, ut ipse interpretatur, significatur Deum subtracturum panis vim alendi. Hierosolymis panem certo pondere comesturos, aquam certa mensura bibituros, carituros lignis. In obsidionibus enim civitatum aut munitionum, si metuenda est fames & annonæ penuria, omnes fruges ad belli duces perferre oportet, qui eas in singula capita certo pondere & mensura

page.notes: The scan is slightly faded at the top left, but the text there is clear. The spelling of the printed text is kept as printed, including "eadem", "siligine" and "Hierosolymis". Changes made per the u/v and i/j rule: "vt" as "ut", "vrbs"/"vrbem" as "urbs"/"urbem", "Ieremias"/"Iudæa"/"Ierusalem"/"iubet" as "Jeremias"/"Judæa"/"Jerusalem"/"jubet". The word "vehementia" and the consonant v in "vesci" and "vim" are kept. The text is a single paragraph, since no paragraph break is printed.
